newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale confirms 1997 higher profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale confirms 1997 higher profit forecast.

text.p: State-owned Aerospatiale reiterated its forecast for a doubling of net profit for 1997, up from 812 million francs for 1996.
Aerospatiale finance director Francois Auque told journalists that 1997 net profit would be around 1.5 billion francs. The group "is profitable on a long-term basis," he said.

Chairman Yves Michot said the group has a target for net profit of five percent of turnover, or 12 percent of capital employed, for each of its branches. The 1997 profit increase reflects the results of a restructuring plan begun in 1995, dollar hedging, and increased deliveries to Airbus Industrie.
Auque said Aerosptiale has a two-year hedge on the dollar at 5.50 francs to the dollar.
The dollar has been trading around 5.80 francs in recent weeks.
Deliveries of Airbus passenger planes for 1998 will virtually be double the 126 aircraft Aerospatiale delivered in 1996, he said.
Aerospatiale made the initial profit forecast in March with its 1996 results, when it said it expected 1997 sales to be around 60 billion francs, up 18 percent from 1996.
Aerospatiale makes missiles, satellites, passenger and regional aircraft, and helicopters.
Airbus is a consortium made up of Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
